text:
Macklin Celebrini is 20, captains the Sharks, plays nearly 23 minutes a night, and the problem in San Jose is not him. He has 18 points in 16 games. San Jose controls 52.8% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on, and his expected-goal share is 12.4 points better than the team's without him, which tells you how hard this roster leans on one player.

The finishing is the quiet part. He's shooting 10.8% against a talent range centred on 14%, with 7 goals on 7.5 expected, so more goals are likelier than fewer. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among 401 forwards at 3.3 wins above replacement, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his 12.8 primary shot assists per 60 in the 99th percentile.

The context is the losing: four straight. After a players-only meeting he kept the message private but said, per Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest, "to a man, we need to be better." For scale, forwards picked in the top three since 2005 scored a median 0.55 points a game in their first full season. He's at 1.12.
headline: Celebrini is fine. The Sharks around him aren't.
